beats.say: Turn on your basement light, and a hunchbacked cricket jumps out of the dark.
No wings, and it can't chirp. But it can jump surprisingly far.
The camel cricket. A humped back, giant back legs, and super long antennae.
Most camel crickets in American homes aren't even from here.
In one study, almost nine out of ten houses with camel crickets had an Asian species.
It first showed up in North America in eighteen ninety eight, in a Minnesota greenhouse.
And for all that jumping, it's completely harmless to you.
It loves cool, damp, dark places. Caves, cellars, basements.
It eats rotting plants, dead insects, and other little bugs.
It grows to about an inch long, not counting the legs.
Scientists asked people across North America to send in photos and specimens.
In ten yards in Raleigh, traps caught a hundred fifty eight. Every one was the Asian species.
The closer to the house, the more they caught.
To keep them out, seal the cracks in your foundation, and around doors and windows.
It usually doesn't breed indoors, unless it stays dark and damp all the time.
Would you go down to that basement?
